source_note: PLACEHOLDER item-analysis thresholds. Every number is invented to make the analyser runnable and MUST be checked against psychometric practice before it is trusted (see docs/TO_VERIFY.md).
min_responses_why: PLACEHOLDER: below this many answers an item's statistics are noise; report INSUFFICIENT_DATA instead of flags.
too_easy_pct_why: PLACEHOLDER: an item almost everyone answers correctly discriminates weakly and wastes session time.
too_hard_pct_why: PLACEHOLDER: an item almost nobody answers correctly is likely mis-keyed or beyond the level.
low_discrimination_why: PLACEHOLDER: discrimination below this (top-group minus bottom-group correctness) means strong and weak students perform alike.
negative_discrimination_why: PLACEHOLDER: a discrimination below this means the top group did WORSE than the bottom group -- almost always a mis-keyed answer.
ambiguous_distractor_pct_why: PLACEHOLDER: a single wrong option chosen by at least this share of students suggests a plausible-but-marked-wrong distractor or a mis-key.
top_bottom_fraction_why: PLACEHOLDER: the classic 27% upper/lower groups used to compute discrimination.
calibration_min_samples_why: PLACEHOLDER: a readiness-vs-grade correlation needs at least this many paired students before it is reported as significant.
